text:
Whether it is worth making an official invitation depends on the degree of risk you are comfortable with. Given they are from Finland (a highly developed, European country) and have visited before without issues, I think the risk of problems is probably very low - I probably wouldn't bother with an invitation if I was in your situation. But if you want to be absolutely sure to avoid problems then you can do the invitation. 

You, as the Israeli, need to do the invite - it is based on the instructions on this page - you would need to print and fill out the form for each person you are inviting and bring them to a PIBA office. https://www.gov.il/he/service/request_for_tourist_visa_b2 Officially you need to submit them at least 20 days in advance, but you should do it much earlier as the offices are slow.  

Note that most of the issues that people have are with parents - their names are recorded in PIBA's databases as part of the visa process and are probably seen to represent a higher risk of settling. I haven't heard of siblings or nieces/nephews having problems at the border due to their connection with a partner-visa holder, so problems for them are probably an even lower risk and so an invitation may be unnecessary.
